messages:
noah: Heads-up: weird auth behavior when creating two AsyncClient instances concurrently. Sometimes both requests show the same API key on the server side. Minimal repro below. Anyone seen this pattern?

rachel: can you paste the repro? async + shared loop can expose global state bugs.

noah: yep - stripped down test (using internal test hook to see which key was used):
```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def call(key, label):
    c = AsyncClient(api_key=key)
    resp = await c._internal_ping()  # returns headers observed by server
    print(label, resp.headers.get('x-used-key'))

async def main():
    await asyncio.gather(call('API_K1', 'one'), call('API_K2', 'two'))

asyncio.run(main())
```
Intermittent output I saw:

one API_K1

two API_K1  # second client used first client's key in this run

vikram: that looks like a shared auth adapter or cached token keyed incorrectly. Do you see the same adapter/transport id for both clients when it fails?

noah: good idea. I printed id(c._auth_adapter) and id(c._transport) and in failing runs the auth_adapter id was identical. Transport was distinct.

anya: sounds like the auth provider factory memoizes by config fingerprint but doesn't account for client instance. If the provider stores mutable state (cached token), sharing it across clients is a footgun.

rachel: short-term workaround: construct each client with an explicit new Transport/AuthAdapter or use an async context manager to scope lifetime so we don't reuse module-level singletons. We should document that in quickstart.

vikram: longer-term fixes for SDK: 1) stop memoizing stateful providers at module level, or make memoization opt-in for stateless providers only; 2) add an explicit bind_credentials flag or an AsyncClient context manager that guarantees instance-scoped auth state; 3) improve type annotations: define a TypedAuthProvider Protocol so mypy flags accidental sharing of providers.

noah: adding a DX suggestion: sample code in notebooks often shows quick constructor usage. If the default encourages shared state, people will hit this. We should add a recommended pattern in devex docs: use "async with AsyncClient(..., bind_credentials=True)" in examples where concurrent clients could be created.

anya: agreed. Also mention precedence rules clearly in docs: constructor api_key > credentials provider instance > REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. That helps triage confusions.

rachel: can you attach a pytest that reproduces the issue intermittently? If we have a flaky test in CI that reproduces it deterministically (e.g., forcing scheduling interleaving), that will speed up the fix.

noah: I'll craft a pytest using asyncio.current_task() yield points to increase collision chance and attach it to the issue.

devex-bot: Created issue #4201: "async sdk: shared auth provider causes multi-client API key leakage" - https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4201 :bug: Labels: devex, bug, needs-repro.

vikram: follow-ups for eng: include client-id in provider cache key if memoization remains, or revert memoization for providers that implement refreshable state. Also add tests for concurrent client scenarios.

rachel: for DX team: I'll draft a short FAQ entry and update quickstart snippets to prefer the context manager pattern. Will add a typing example for TypedAuthProvider too.

noah: thanks all. tagging @vikram for the PR when it's ready. I'll post the pytest and a small log snippet in the new issue. :thumbsup:
